city.transit_summary: S-Bahn (elevated rail), U-Bahn (subway), Tram (M-Metrotram), BVG Bus. Standard zone AB covers all walking stops. Single ticket is €3.50; 24-hour AB pass is €9.90. Validate stamped paper tickets before boarding.
anchors_confirmed: Berlin Wall at the East Side Gallery

practical_notes.title: Sunday and Holiday Closures (Sonntagsruhe)
practical_notes.short_text: Retail shops, supermarkets, and pharmacies are closed on Sundays by German federal law. Museums and cafes stay open.
practical_notes.longer_text: Except for designated travel stations (Hauptbahnhof, Friedrichstraße, Ostbahnhof), retail shops close strictly on Sundays. State museums and memorial sites operate normally on Sundays but typically observe Ruhetag (closing day) on Mondays. Bakeries and cafes generally open Sunday mornings.

practical_notes.title: Cash Culture & Tipping (Trinkgeld)
practical_notes.short_text: Carry €20–€50 cash. Smaller Imbiss stands, bakeries, and kiosks often do not accept cards.
practical_notes.longer_text: While contactless card payment is widely accepted in sit-down restaurants, cash remains king for street food, beer gardens, public WC fees, and flea markets. When tipping in cafes and restaurants, round up by 5–10% and tell the server the total amount before handing over cash or paying by card (e.g., if the bill is €18.20, say 'zwanzig bitte' for €20). Do not leave tips on the table.

practical_notes.title: Public Toilets (City-WC) & Drinking Water
practical_notes.short_text: Berlin 'City-Toilette' booths cost €0.50 (card/contactless or coins). Tap water is safe.
practical_notes.longer_text: Automated City-WC booths are located near major plazas and stations. Station toilets (Sanifair) cost €1.00 with a partial discount voucher. Tap water across Berlin has mineral-rich drinking quality. Bottled drinks carry a 'Pfand' deposit (€0.08–€0.25) refundable when returning empties to any supermarket Pfandautomat.

practical_notes.title: Essential German Walking Phrases
practical_notes.short_text: Polite greetings and ordering basics with clear phonetic hints.
practical_notes.longer_text:
'Guten Tag' (GOO-ten tahk) - Hello / Good day
'Bitte' (BIT-tuh) - Please / You are welcome
'Danke' (DAHN-kuh) - Thank you
'Einmal Currywurst bitte' (EYEN-mahl KOOR-ee-voorst BIT-tuh) - One Currywurst, please
'Zahlen bitte' (TSAH-len BIT-tuh) - The bill, please
'Stimmt so' (SHTIMT zoh) - Keep the change

walks.title: Mitte Essentials: Gate, Island and Cathedral
walks.editorial_introduction: The quintessential Berlin walk for your first day. Moves from the Cold War gate through Prussian neoclassical boulevard Unter den Linden to the UNESCO Museum Island and Cathedral, ending at Hackescher Markt. No rushing, zero backtrack.
walks.who_will_love_it: First-time visitors wanting an unhurried, panoramic walk connecting Berlin's iconic historical spine.
walks.who_should_pick_another: Travellers seeking gritty counter-culture or modern club neighborhoods; pick the Kreuzberg walk instead.
walks.elevation: Flat throughout; gentle ramps around Lustgarten bridge.
walks.surfaces: Smooth asphalt and granite paving; minor historical cobbles at Pariser Platz.
walks.start_transit: Brandenburger Tor (S-Bahn S1/S2/S25/S26, U-Bahn U5) — exit toward Pariser Platz
walks.end_transit: Hackescher Markt (S-Bahn S3/S5/S7/S9) or U5 Museumsinsel

nearest_stations_by_stop.reichstag-exterior: Bundestag U5 (250m) or S+U Brandenburger Tor (400m)

walks.best_time_of_day: Morning (09:30–12:30) or late afternoon golden hour.
walks.weather_variant_note: If rain begins, the walk shortens comfortably at Museum Island with extensive sheltered colonnades and indoor museum lobbies.

food_positions.context_note: Placed along the Linden stretch just before crossing to Museum Island for fresh pastry, tea, or chocolate.
Sits at the walk finish beside Hackescher Markt station, perfect for lunch or coffee with tired feet.

walks.title: Cold War Borderlines & Eastward River Finish
walks.editorial_introduction: Traces the divided city from Potsdamer Platz through the Gestapo ruins and Checkpoint Charlie, offering a dedicated eastward transit or river transition to the 1.3 km painted Wall at the East Side Gallery.
walks.who_will_love_it: Anyone keen to understand how the Wall cut through everyday life and how the Spree riverfront transformed.
walks.who_should_pick_another: Travellers on a strict 2-hour schedule who dislike taking a brief train leg; the East Side Gallery is a deliberate eastward extension.
walks.elevation: Virtually flat; slight grade onto Oberbaumbrücke.
walks.surfaces: Broad concrete pavement, gravel path at Topography of Terror, paved riverside promenade.
walks.start_transit: Potsdamer Platz (S-Bahn / U-Bahn U2) — exit Stresemannstraße
walks.end_transit: Warschauer Straße (S-Bahn S3/S5/S7/S9, U-Bahn U1/U3) or Ostbahnhof
walks.best_time_of_day: Early afternoon (13:30–16:30), allows clear sunlight on the East Side Gallery murals.
walks.weather_variant_note: Topography of Terror documentation center is completely indoors and free. If storm hits at Checkpoint Charlie, hop on U6 to avoid exposed river walk.

food_positions.context_note: A traditional quick bite stop for Berlin currywurst and fries before the eastward transit connection.
Warm, sheltered courtyard cafe right by Warschauer Straße station at the walk finish.

walks.title: Kreuzberg Flavours & Landwehr Canal
walks.editorial_introduction: An intimate neighbourhood walk diving into SO36's lively immigrant heritage, independent bakeries, the historic Markthalle Neun market, and the weeping willow promenade along the Landwehr Canal.
walks.who_will_love_it: Food lovers, people watchers, and anyone wanting genuine neighbourhood vibrancy away from tour buses.
walks.who_should_pick_another: Travellers focused solely on textbook monuments and Prussian architecture.
walks.surfaces: Pavement, packed dirt path along canal, arched iron bridge steps (ramp available).
walks.start_transit: Kottbusser Tor (U-Bahn U1/U3/U8) — exit Reichenberger Straße
walks.best_time_of_day: Thursday late afternoon (Street Food Thursday) or Saturday midday.
walks.weather_variant_note: Markthalle Neun provides 3,000 square meters of roofed market hall shelter with seating and coffee.

food_positions.context_note: Fresh wood-fired lahmacun and freshly grilled skewers made right in front of you.
Artisan butcher stall inside the market serving pastrami or German craft burger, eaten at communal wooden tables.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: Berlin's sole surviving 18th-century neoclassical city gate, crowned by Schadow's copper Quadriga of the goddess of victory in a four-horse chariot.
stops.why_it_matters: Commissioned in 1791 by King Frederick William II as a symbol of peace, it stood trapped in the forbidden Death Strip for 28 years until the Wall fell on November 9, 1989.
stops.what_to_notice: Look beneath your feet at the double row of cobblestones cutting across the square: that exact line marks the path of the Berlin Wall.
stops.local_tip: Stand inside the central passage. During the royal era, only the monarch's carriage was permitted to pass through the middle portal.
stops.step_free_notes: Pariser Platz is completely flat and paved with smooth granite flagstones.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: The seat of the German Bundestag (Parliament), famous for its 1894 neo-Renaissance facade combined with Sir Norman Foster's transparent glass dome.
stops.why_it_matters: Burned in 1933, battered in 1945, and wrapped in silver fabric by Christo in 1995, its 1999 revival symbolizes a transparent, reunited democratic Germany.
stops.what_to_notice: The inscription above the western pediment reads 'DEM DEUTSCHEN VOLKE' (To the German People), cast from melted French cannon bronze in 1916.
stops.local_tip: Exterior viewing on this walk is completely open and free. Entering the glass dome requires free registration weeks in advance via the official Bundestag portal — no app or guide can bypass this.
stops.opening_hours: Exterior view 24/7. Official building open by appointment only.
stops.step_free_notes: Platz der Republik is a level paved plaza with wheelchair accessible ramps.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: Berlin's historic grand boulevard, lined with four rows of linden (lime) trees running 1.5 km from the Gate east to the Schlossbrücke.
stops.why_it_matters: Originally laid out in 1647 to connect the City Palace to the Tiergarten hunting grounds, it became the architectural stage of the Enlightenment and Prussian empire.
stops.what_to_notice: The bronze equestrian statue of Frederick the Great gazing east, and the subtle underground glass window at Bebelplatz showing empty white bookshelves commemorating the 1933 Nazi book burnings.
stops.local_tip: Walk straight down the broad gravel pedestrian median under the trees rather than the roadside sidewalks for the cleanest breeze and best view.
stops.step_free_notes: Fine packed gravel median and wide level curb cutouts throughout.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: A northern tip of the Spree Island holding five world-class museums built between 1824 and 1930, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage cultural complex.
stops.why_it_matters: Conceived by Prussian visionaries as a 'sanctuary for art and science', each building was constructed to showcase a specific epoch of human civilization.
stops.what_to_notice: The bullet pockmarks and shrapnel scars still visible on the stone colonnades and fluted pillars along the Bodestraße canal bank.
stops.local_tip: If choosing to enter just one on a walking day, pick the Neues Museum to see the 3,300-year-old bust of Nefertiti. Note that state museums close Mondays.
stops.opening_hours: Courtyards and river gardens open daily 08:00–22:00. Museum buildings 10:00–18:00.
stops.step_free_notes: River promenades and Lustgarten have ramped bridge crossings and level flagstones.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: Berlin's monumental High Renaissance / Baroque revival Protestant church, dominated by a massive 98-meter dome flanked by the Spree river and the Lustgarten park.
stops.why_it_matters: Completed in 1905 under Kaiser Wilhelm II as the imperial dynastic church and Hohenzollern burial vault, opposing St. Peter's Basilica in Rome.
stops.what_to_notice: The 70-ton granite bowl in the middle of Lustgarten, carved in 1828 from a single glacial erratic boulder found in Brandenburg.
stops.local_tip: Rest your feet on the Lustgarten lawn. The walk concludes here, just 400 meters across the bridge from Hackescher Markt S-Bahn station.
stops.opening_hours: Park grounds open 24/7. Cathedral interior visits €10 (Mon–Sat 10:00–17:00, Sun 12:00–17:00).
stops.step_free_notes: Park paths and bridge footpaths are step-free; Cathedral interior has wheelchair lift at north gate.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: Europe's busiest pre-war traffic interchange, turned into an erased Cold War no-man's land, and reborn after 1990 as a showcase of bold modern architecture.
stops.why_it_matters: During the 1920s it had Europe's first traffic light. From 1961 to 1989 it was completely empty sand and razor wire; after reunification it became Europe's biggest construction site.
stops.what_to_notice: The preserved segments of the Wall standing upright right outside the S-Bahn pavilion, often covered with chewing gum and historic notes.
stops.local_tip: Look at the brass strip embedded in the pavement marking the Wall's zig-zag line directly across the roadway.
stops.step_free_notes: Paved and level pedestrian zone with underground elevators to train platforms.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: The excavated basement ruins of the Reich Security Main Office, Gestapo, and SS headquarters, alongside a 200-meter original stretch of the outer Berlin Wall.
stops.why_it_matters: From this exact site, the instruments of Nazi state terror and the Holocaust were organized and commanded between 1933 and 1945.
stops.what_to_notice: The exposed brick cellars along Niederkirchnerstraße where political prisoners were interrogated and tortured.
stops.local_tip: Both the outdoor trench exhibition and the indoor documentation center are completely free of charge. Quiet contemplation is respected here.
stops.step_free_notes: Ramped walkways down to the trench and smooth indoor pavilion.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: The replica American guardhouse and famous border sign ('YOU ARE LEAVING THE AMERICAN SECTOR') in the middle of Friedrichstraße.
stops.why_it_matters: The sole crossing point for foreigners, diplomats, and Allied military personnel between East and West Berlin, and the site of the dramatic October 1961 US-Soviet tank standoff.
stops.what_to_notice: The two-sided lightbox portrait above the street: one side shows an American soldier, the other a Soviet soldier, facing their respective sectors.
stops.local_tip: Ignore the actors charging for fake passport stamps; instead, read the excellent open-air photo timeline panels standing on the corner of Zimmerstraße.
stops.step_free_notes: Standard asphalt city sidewalks and curb cuts.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: The longest contiguous surviving segment of the Berlin Wall (1,316 meters), painted in spring 1990 by 118 artists from 21 countries.
stops.why_it_matters: Unlike the western graffiti-covered wall, this was the eastern 'Hinterlandmauer' facing East Berlin, painted immediately after the border opened as a monument to freedom.
stops.what_to_notice: Dmitri Vrubel's iconic 'Fraternal Kiss' between Leonid Brezhnev and Erich Honecker, and Birgit Kinder's Trabant crashing through concrete.
stops.local_tip: Walk along the Spree river side of the wall for scenic water views, or along Mühlenstraße to view all 101 historic murals.
stops.step_free_notes: Level, wide concrete sidewalk running the entire 1.3 km length.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: A striking double-deck red brick Gothic revival bridge with dual towers crossing the Spree between Kreuzberg and Friedrichshain.
stops.why_it_matters: During the Cold War, this was a heavily fortified pedestrian border crossing for West Berliners. Today the yellow U1 subway train rumbles across its upper arches.
stops.what_to_notice: The stone water-gate towers modelled on historic medieval city defenses and the view of the 'Molecule Man' sculpture upstream.
stops.local_tip: Stand inside the covered pedestrian arcade on the west side of the bridge as the yellow U-Bahn train rattles overhead.
stops.step_free_notes: Paved sidewalks across the bridge; ramped approaches from both river banks.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: The vibrant urban epicenter of Kreuzberg, surrounded by 1970s social housing blocks (Neues Kreuzberger Zentrum) and bustling Turkish markets.
stops.why_it_matters: A living symbol of West Berlin's post-war Turkish guest-worker community and Kreuzberg's vibrant community activism.
stops.what_to_notice: The elevated yellow U-Bahn track cutting through the center of the square and the aroma of roasted sesame, cumin, and fresh mint.
stops.local_tip: Keep your wallet secure in your front pocket, grab a fresh simit (sesame bread ring) from a bakery cart, and head east into Oranienstraße.
stops.step_free_notes: Paved street level; elevator available inside Kottbusser Tor U-Bahn station.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: Kreuzberg's famed independent high street, packed with bookstores, record shops, record cafes, and political community spaces.
stops.why_it_matters: The historic heart of Berlin's punk, squatter, and alternative arts movement from the late 1970s onward.
stops.what_to_notice: The courtyard passages (Höfe) off the street concealing peaceful ateliers and small roast cafes.
stops.local_tip: Duck into the courtyard of Oranienstraße 25 to visit the historic Buchhandlung Kisch & Co bookstore.
stops.step_free_notes: Sidewalks are mostly smooth flagstones; some courtyard thresholds have 1-2 steps.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: One of 14 historic covered market halls built in Berlin in 1891, restored as a bustling hub of regional produce, artisan bread, and street cuisine.
stops.why_it_matters: Saved by neighborhood citizens from being sold to a discount supermarket chain in 2009, it sparked Germany's modern artisanal food renaissance.
stops.what_to_notice: The ornate 19th-century cast-iron roof trusses supporting the cavernous central market hall.
stops.local_tip: On Thursdays 17:00–22:00, it hosts Street Food Thursday with global bites. On regular days, visit before 16:00 for fresh bread and coffee.
stops.step_free_notes: Completely level ground-floor hall with accessible automatic side doors on Eisenbahnstraße.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: A leafy pedestrian and bicycle promenade running along the willow-draped banks of the historic 1852 Landwehr Canal.
stops.why_it_matters: Once an industrial coal-transport canal, today it serves as Kreuzberg's outdoor living room and community meeting ground.
stops.what_to_notice: Locals playing boules (pétanque) under the chestnut trees beside the gentle canal water.
stops.local_tip: Grab an ice cream from a waterfront parlor and sit on the grassy embankment facing the south-facing sun.
stops.step_free_notes: Packed gravel and smooth asphalt promenade with level access throughout.

stops.what_am_i_looking_at: Berlin's oldest wrought-iron arch bridge over the Landwehr Canal, completed in 1882 with open balustrades and street bollards.
stops.why_it_matters: The beloved communal sunset spot where Kreuzbergers gather with drinks, guitars, and chatter on mild evenings.
stops.what_to_notice: The decorative historic iron filigree and the wide cobblestone approach curbs where walkers lounge at dusk.
stops.local_tip: Acoustic music curfew is 22:00 out of respect for neighbors. Walk 350 meters southwest to Schönleinstraße U-Bahn to conclude the walk.
stops.step_free_notes: Slight ramped incline over the bridge with paved walkways.

route_legs.plain_instruction: From Pariser Platz, head north through Ebertstraße and follow the tree-lined path into Platz der Republik. The Reichstag's glass dome will be immediately ahead on your right.
route_legs.surface_notes: Wide smooth asphalt promenade; zero steps.

route_legs.plain_instruction: Turn south back past the Gate and cross Wilhelmstraße onto the wide tree-lined gravel promenade in the center of Unter den Linden.
route_legs.surface_notes: Granite sidewalks and fine packed gravel median under the trees.
route_legs.indoor_alternative: Underground passages of U5 Brandenburger Tor if heavy deluge.

route_legs.plain_instruction: Continue straight east past Humboldt University and Bebelplatz. Cross Schlossbrücke (Castle Bridge) across the Spree canal onto Museum Island.
route_legs.surface_notes: Flat stone bridge and wide pedestrian crosswalks.
route_legs.indoor_alternative: Humboldt Forum ground floor passage provides warm, sheltered throughway.

route_legs.plain_instruction: Walk across Lustgarten lawn directly toward the massive green-copper dome of the Cathedral.
route_legs.surface_notes: Level gravel park path and stone steps (ramp available on cathedral left).
route_legs.indoor_alternative: Sheltered colonnade behind the Altes Museum.

route_legs.plain_instruction: Head southeast down Stresemannstraße and turn left onto Niederkirchnerstraße. The preserved outer Wall and exposed basement ruins are on your right.
route_legs.surface_notes: Standard city sidewalk, packed crushed stone pathway along the Wall memorial.

route_legs.plain_instruction: Continue east along Niederkirchnerstraße as it becomes Zimmerstraße, until you reach the bustling Friedrichstraße cross street. The white guardhouse stands in the center.
route_legs.surface_notes: Smooth pavement and marked pedestrian crossings.

route_legs.plain_instruction: EASTWARD EXTENSION CHOICE: Either take the scenic 45-minute pedestrian path east along the Spree riverbanks, OR hop on U-Bahn U6 at Kochstraße north to Stadtmitte then U2/S-Bahn east to Warschauer Straße (12 mins). The East Side Gallery stretches along Mühlenstraße toward the river.
route_legs.surface_notes: Paved riverside path or transit option for tired feet.
route_legs.indoor_alternative: Transit link: U-Bahn U6 to Stadtmitte then U2/S-Bahn to Warschauer Straße.

route_legs.plain_instruction: Follow the painted wall murals east to the river bend. The red-brick towers of the Oberbaumbrücke rise directly ahead over the water.
route_legs.surface_notes: Broad concrete pavement and covered arcade walkway on the bridge.

route_legs.plain_instruction: Exit Kotti heading east along Oranienstraße, passing small bakeries and cafes on both sides.
Walk east on Oranienstraße, turn right on Manteuffelstraße, then left into Eisenbahnstraße. The entrance to Markthalle Neun is marked by cast-iron gates.
Head south down Eisenbahnstraße to the water's edge of the Landwehr Canal. Turn right onto the tree-shaded Paul-Lincke-Ufer promenade.
route_legs.surface_notes: Packed dirt and gravel footpath along the canal.

route_legs.plain_instruction: Stroll westward under the weeping willows beside the canal until you reach the curved iron railings of the historic Admiralbrücke.
route_legs.surface_notes: Gravel canal path and stone bridge paving.
